hints: Focus on the charges of the metal ions formed, since carboxylate salts must balance the positive charge on the metal.
Notice that $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ are both 2+ ions, so each needs two $\text{RCOO}^-$ ions to make a neutral salt.
Check the balancing of atoms as well as the salt formulae, then decide which equation has both a correct formula and a balanced equation.
walkthrough:
**Recall what carboxylic acids do**

Think of $\text{RCOOH}$ as a typical acid. It reacts with carbonates to give salt + $\text{CO}_2$ + water, with metals to give salt + $\text{H}_2$, and with bases to give salt + water.

General idea:
$$\text{RCOOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- \text{ (in the salt)}$$

**Check equation 1**

Magnesium forms $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, so it needs two ethanoate ions: $(\text{CH}_3\text{COO})_2\text{Mg}$.

The equation shows $\text{CH}_3\text{COOMg}$, which has the wrong formula and is not balanced. So 1 is incorrect.

**Check equation 2**

Sodium forms $\text{Na}^+$, so one propanoate ion gives the neutral salt $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{Na} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2$$
This is correctly balanced for H and all other atoms. So 2 is correct.

**Check equation 3**

Barium forms $\text{Ba}^{2+}$, so it needs two propanoate ions: $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO})_2\text{Ba}$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOBa}_2$.

The correct reaction needs 2 acids for one $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$:
$$2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{Ba(OH)}_2 \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO})_2\text{Ba} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So 3 has the wrong formula and wrong balancing. So 3 is incorrect.

**Conclude**

Only 2 is correct. That matches the option for 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect. While 2 is correct, 1 and 3 both show wrong salt formulae for 2+ metals. $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ needs $(\text{CH}_3\text{COO})_2\text{Mg}$ and $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ needs $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO})_2\text{Ba}$.
options.B: Incorrect. 2 is correct, but 1 is wrong. Students often spot the familiar acid + carbonate products and forget to check that Mg needs two carboxylate groups to balance its 2+ charge.
options.C: Correct. Only 2 has both the right salt formula, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa}$, and correct balancing with $\tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2$. Equations 1 and 3 fail because they do not balance the 2+ charge of Mg and Ba.
options.D: Incorrect. Equation 3 looks like neutralisation, but the salt formula $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOBa}_2$ is backwards. The Ba should be one ion with two carboxylates, and the mole ratio should be 2 acid : 1 base.
